draft.title: Simple and compound interest
card: Simple interest
The same dollar amount is added each period, found from the starting amount only. Interest per period = P × r, where P is the principal and r is the rate per period as a decimal.
Compound interest
Interest is a percentage of the current balance, so it grows as the balance grows. Each period the balance is multiplied by 1 + r.
Recurrence rules: simple interest is V(n+1) = V(n) + P × r. Compound interest is V(n+1) = (1 + r) × V(n).
draft.remember: Simple adds the same dollars each period. Compound multiplies the balance each period.

a.q: Which recurrence rule models $800 invested at 4% per year compound interest?
a.why: Compound interest multiplies the balance by 1 + 0.04 = 1.04 each year. V(n) + 32 is the rule for simple interest, because it adds the same amount each year. 0.04 × V(n) would leave only the interest, not the whole balance.
a.clue: The balance is multiplied each year, and the old balance is kept.

b.q: Priya invests $5000 at 6% per year simple interest. What is the balance after 3 years?
b.why: Simple interest is 5000 × 0.06 = $300 each year. Over 3 years that is $900, so the balance is $5900. $5954.08 is the compound answer, because 5000 × 1.06³ is about 5955.08 and not the same sum added each year. $5300 is only one year of interest.
b.clue: Add the same dollar amount every year, found from the starting $5000.

problems.detail: The distractor $5954.08 is meant to be the compound-interest answer, but 5000 × 1.06³ = $5955.08. The why gives 5955.08 while naming the $5954.08 option, so it contradicts itself. Change the option to $5955.08 so the why holds.
